Think of your immune system like a security team that protects your body. It has special soldiers, called white blood cells, that can spot and destroy germs like viruses and bacteria.

A vaccine gives your immune system a “practice drill.” It shows it a harmless piece of a germ, or a weakened version, without making you seriously sick.

During that practice, your immune system learns what the germ looks like and makes special tools called antibodies to fight it.
